dialog.body: Public Works, this is Lorraine, how can I help you this afternoon?
Hi Lorraine. Yeah, I'd like to report an indoor swimming pool. Except it's my basement, and nobody asked for it. Twice now.
Oh no. Okay, you've got water in the basement?

Had. Had water. We pumped most of it out yesterday. But I'm calling because this is the second time this winter, and the first time we called, you guys came out, and it didn't fix anything. So I'm hoping we can do it right this time.
Okay. Let me get your name and the address first and I'll pull up whatever we've got.
Daniel Haddad. H-A-D-D-A-D. The house is six Brewer Street, Fifth Ward, right near the corner.

Daniel Haddad, H-A-D-D-A-D, six Brewer Street. Give me one second. [pause] Okay, yup, I see it. There's a report from... January twelfth, a drain backup at the corner, and then another note on the thirteenth.

Right. The twelfth was me. The thirteenth, that was my mother Leila, she called that evening after the crew left. Because the crew came, pulled a clump of leaves and a plastic bag off the grate, and drove away. That was it. That was the whole visit.
I see that. It says grate cleared on the thirteenth, and then it was flagged for a supervisor to take a look.
Flagged. Okay. Did a supervisor ever look?
I'm not seeing anything after that note, no.

Yeah. That's what I figured, because nobody ever called us. My mother asked them that night, who can look under the street, because it's not the grate, the grate's not the problem. And then two weeks go by, nothing, and here we are.
Okay. So tell me about this one. This was the storm Sunday into Monday?

Yeah, the snow that turned to rain. Sunday it's snowing, and then overnight it goes over to rain and everything's melting at once. I came downstairs Monday morning, the twenty-sixth, and there's water all over the basement floor. Came in the exact same spot as the first time. The foundation wall seam on the corner side. Same seam, same corner, just more of it.
Same entry point as the first time, the seam in the foundation wall on the corner side. How deep did it get?
About eight inches.
Sorry, you're breaking up a little, was that eighteen?
No, no. Eight. E-I-G-H-T. Eight inches. First time was four, this time eight. So it's getting worse, not better.
Eight inches, okay, got it. And the first one was four. I'm writing that down.

And here's the other thing. When I went out Monday morning to look at the street, the manhole down by the corner, the cover was bubbling. Water was coming up through the holes in the cover, like a pot boiling over. So it's not like the water's got nowhere to go because of some leaves. It's coming back up out of the pipe.
Water coming up through the manhole cover near the corner. Okay. That's helpful, actually, that tells them it's more than the grate.

Right, that's what I've been saying. That's what my mother said two weeks ago. And it's not just us. The neighbor up the street had water in their basement too. Both times. Same two storms. So whatever's under that corner, it's backing up into more than one house.
A neighbor on Brewer had water both times as well. Okay. Did they call in, do you know?
I don't know if they did. I told them they should. But I'm telling you, so now you know.
No, I appreciate that, I'll put it in the notes. And what got damaged on your end? Same things as before, or anything new?

Same stuff. It's an unfinished basement, it's just storage. The dehumidifier got wet again, which is kind of funny if you think about it, the dehumidifier drowning. The shelving, and the holiday decorations, which we'd just finished drying out from the first time. So nothing new, just the same stuff getting soaked all over again. Which, you know, that's the point. The same thing happened twice and nobody fixed it.
Dehumidifier, shelving, holiday decorations, all wet again, nothing additional. Okay.

Look, Lorraine, I know it's not you personally. I know the crews were out all over the place after this storm. But I called, we did what we were supposed to do, somebody came out and did basically nothing, and somebody said a supervisor would look and nobody looked. And now I've got eight inches in the basement. At some point I'm going to have to call a lawyer, because I don't know what else gets anybody's attention.

I understand. I hear you. What I can do right now is put this in as a repeat backup, not a new one, so it's tied to the first report and they can see the history. And I want to get a crew out to actually look at the line under the corner, not just the grate.
Okay. When?
Let me look at the schedule. [pause] I can get them out there Thursday. Thursday the twenty-ninth.
Thursday. And they're going to look under the street this time? Not just pick up a bag and leave?

I'm writing in the order, in plain words, grate was already cleared January thirteenth, problem continued, manhole bubbling up at the corner, repeat flooding at six Brewer and a neighbor. Check the line under the corner. That way whoever shows up knows the grate isn't the answer.
Okay. That's better. That's what should've happened the first time.
And then I'm also requesting a supervisor callback, and I'm putting a date on it this time. You should hear from a supervisor by Friday, the thirtieth.
By Friday. Okay. I'll hold you to it. Not you, but, you know. Somebody.
That's fair. What's the best number for the supervisor to reach you?
My cell. Four oh one, five five five, [line breaks up] two.
I lost the end of that, could you say it one more time?
Yeah, sorry, I'm out back. Four, oh, one. Five, five, five. Oh, one, seven, two.
Four oh one, five five five, zero one seven two.
Zero one seven two, that's it. Oh one seven two.

Got it. So let me read the whole thing back to you so we're on the same page. Daniel Haddad, six Brewer Street. Basement flooded the second time this winter, overnight Sunday into Monday, the twenty-sixth. Water came in through the same foundation wall seam on the corner side as the first flood, about eight inches. Manhole at the corner was bubbling up through the cover. Neighbor on the street had water both times. Dehumidifier, shelving, and holiday decorations wet again, nothing new. Crew Thursday the twenty-ninth to check the line under the corner, supervisor callback by Friday the thirtieth at four oh one, five five five, zero one seven two.
Yeah. That's all of it. Thank you for actually writing it all down.
Of course. And if it rains again before Thursday and you get anything coming in, call us right away, don't wait. Same thing with the manhole, if it starts coming up again, call that in.

Oh, I'll call. Believe me. I'm not trying to be a pain, I just don't want to be standing in my basement in two weeks having this same conversation. Because if there's a third time, I'm done being polite about it, I'm going straight to the lawyer.
I understand. The note's in there, it's tied to the earlier reports, and the crew's on for Thursday.
Alright. Thursday. Thanks, Lorraine.
You're welcome, Mr. Haddad. Take care, and good luck with the drying out.
Yeah, the decorations have had a rough month. Bye.
